newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean defector to stay in Philippines in March.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean defector to stay in Philippines in March.

text.p: Top North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop will stay in the Philippines at least until the start of next month, a senior South Korean official said on Thursday.
Hwang, the most senior North Korean official to flee the Stalinist nation, has been in the Philippines since he flew from Beijing on Tuesday, but his exact whereabouts has remained secret.

"China and South Korea have agreed on how long Hwang will have to stay in the Philippines. He will not be able to travel to South Korea within this month," the official, from South Korea's Foreign Ministry, told Reuters.
President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday that Hwang could stay in the Philippines "only for as long as necessary and as short as possible".
Hwang sought political asylum in South Korea's consulate in Beijing on February 12 and stayed there until China agreed to let him go to Seoul via Manila.

"The Philippine government has agreed to accommodate the Seoul-Beijing agreement on the length of Hwang's stay in the Philippines," said the Seoul official, speaking anonymously. He declined to elaborate.
The defection of Hwang, North Korea's top ideologue and ranked 24th in Pyongyang's hierarchy, forced Beijing to make an agonising choice.
China eventually came down on the side of wealthy investment partner Seoul by letting Hwang go -- but insisted that the asylum seeker would have to stay in a third country "for a considerable time".

Diplomats said Hwang's detour through the Philippines would help Pyongyang, China's ideological ally, save face while reassuring Seoul that its prize catch would be out of easy reach of Northern agents.
North Korea, which has a history of deadly attacks against arch-rival South Korea, does not have an embassy in the Philippines.
South Korean President Kim Young-sam has sent letters thanking Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng for letting Hwang leave Beijing, Kim's spokesman said on Thursday.
